leads.title: Grid equipment capacity relief versus backlog pressure
leads.hypothesis: A source-dated change in qualified grid-equipment capacity relative to backlog pressure may create an event lead, but only if a separate observable market prior can later be bound.
leads.bottleneck_node: Qualified high-voltage transformer and switchgear manufacturing capacity
leads.supply_response_lag: Factory expansion, qualification and utility acceptance require multiple reporting periods.
causal_chain: Grid interconnection and replacement demand reaches constrained equipment categories.
Qualified manufacturing capacity responds with a long commissioning and acceptance lag.
Source-dated backlog and capacity disclosures can reveal whether pressure is tightening or easing.
An investable claim remains unidentified until the disclosure is compared with a pre-event market prior.

source_groups.independence_basis: A public energy-agency publication is institutionally separate from issuer disclosures.
source_groups.evidence_summary: Official infrastructure material describes demand and procurement pressure without ranking securities.

sources.authorization_basis: Public federal material; exact reuse and automated-access terms still require run-specific confirmation.
sources.pit_basis: The template does not bind an immutable first-public-availability timestamp.

source_groups.independence_basis: Issuer filings originate from reporting companies rather than the demand-side agency.
source_groups.evidence_summary: Issuer filings can describe backlog, capacity projects and counterevidence about supply adequacy.

sources.publisher: United States Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.authorization_basis: Public filing reuse is possible, while fair-access, archive and strategy-use details remain a source preflight obligation.
sources.pit_basis: Acceptance time alone is not asserted to be a provable tradable decision timestamp.

counterevidence.statement: Some issuers state that current or planned capacity is adequate for expected demand.
counterevidence.implication: A broad structural shortage story is insufficient; the lead must abstain when capacity relief is already visible.

market_expectation.description: No same-cohort, strictly pre-event consensus or price-revealed prior is bound in this template.

leads.why_not_arbitraged: Product scope, metric comparability, qualification and disclosure clocks are costly to align, but that complexity is only a hypothesis until a market prior is observed.
leads.falsifier: Reject the lead if the source-use or PIT contract fails, the apparent pressure is explained by mix or acquisition effects, or no independent market-prior surface can be bound.

baseline.policy: Current cash-feasible strategy without a bottleneck mechanism score.

treatment.policy: Research-only extraction of source-dated bottleneck state; no order, ranking or strategy rule.

leads.replacement_value_comparator: Cash, SPY, QQQ, same-industry peers and the exact core candidate that would later be displaced.

execution_envelope.liquidity_dependency: Must be declared in a later candidate contract
execution_envelope.costs_and_carry: Must be declared in a later candidate contract
execution_envelope.capacity_constraint: No notional allocation at lead generation
execution_envelope.timing_constraint: All source and prior timestamps must precede any later decision clock

leads.source_preflight_next_action: Verify source authorization, immutable PIT provenance and same-cohort market-prior availability without reading candidate outcomes or reserving an experiment.

reopen_condition.condition: At least two authorized independent source groups and one observable pre-event prior are bound to existing registered surfaces.

history_vetoes.reason: Template placeholder: a real run must perform the repository history veto only after freezing the generated lead.
